chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about wine, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent me as a mercy to the worlds, and to obliterate the musical instruments, and the pipes, and the affairs of the Pre-Islamic period, and the idols.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'My Lord swore that no servant of Mine will drink wine in the world except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished or forgiven; and no servant of Mine will give it to a young child or a slave except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished afterwards or forgiven.'

key_terms.الْحَمِيم: Scalding water (a specific drink in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment for drinking wine mentioned in this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who attributes the prohibition of wine to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), framing it as part of eradicating Jahiliyyah customs like music and idols. The hadith highlights a specific divine vow (qasam Allah) where the drinker is quenched with an equivalent measure of scalding water (hamim) on the Day of Judgment, illustrating the principle of proportional retribution (muqabalah) in divine justice.
